rv.q: The show has fully developed characters, a strong cast and a new story to tell in an old-fashioned way.
The result is Allegiance, a somewhat ungainly musical that has moments of beauty and passion, as well as a complexity of themes that are not the usual stuff of Broadway shows.

Even if it’s not 100 percent original all the time (hey, not everything can be Hamilton), Allegiance is an important show with a phenomenal cast, and it deserves to be seen.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this Japanese internment camp musical: many praise its important subject matter and heartfelt performances (especially Takei and Salonga), but fault the conventional score and heavy-handed storytelling.

vs.sum: The Longacre Theatre offers good sightlines with minimal obstructions, even from the balcony, and the sound quality is consistently praised. While the seating is a bit narrow, it provides average comfort for most patrons. The theater's ambiance is enhanced by its elegant Beaux Arts interior, and facilities are typical for a Broadway venue, with some lines at intermission but generally manageable.

acc.note: Small restroom-only elevator (may not accommodate all wheelchairs). 3 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra.
